findings.title: Compilation source is unresolved, and reading from `.claude/` cannot work on a Copilot-only project
findings.description: The file layout says outputs come "from `.claude/rules/typescript.md`" and "from `.claude/skills/commit.md`", while line 114 names no source at all. `.claude/` is the output of the claude target. On the plan's fresh-directory flow (`cf init --ide copilot`, plan line 212) it does not exist, and line 17 forbids the copilot target from creating it. The code comment at `packages/cli/src/commands/setup-ide.ts:111-121` says the script compiles from the guides submodule source. The design must name the guide-side source directory and drop the `.claude/` wording, or the driving user (no Claude at all) gets empty output.

findings.title: Skills layout claim is wrong and skill→prompt frontmatter translation is not specified
Existing CLAUDE.md safety block is not target-gated and will fire for `copilot`
Unmanaged-file protection covers two of four outputs; prompt and backup semantics are unspecified
Declining the prompt still propagates to worktrees
findings.description: On "N", `setupIdeAction` prints "Aborted." and returns normally (`:78-81`). The command handler then calls `propagateToWorktrees` unconditionally. With the copilot block added, a user who declines to overwrite their own root `AGENTS.md` and `.github/` files gets those unmanaged files copied over every registered worktree's copies. The design's sequence (lines 98-102) does not say what a decline does. It needs an explicit "abort skips propagation" signal, such as a boolean return.

findings.title: Marker helper is named and typed two different ways, and duplicates an existing generic function
findings.description: Line 29 specifies `isManagedCopilot(filePath)`; line 109 specifies `isManagedCopilotFiles(projectPath)`. These differ in name, parameter and implied return shape. Neither is needed: `isManagedClaudeMd(filePath)` at `setup-ide.ts:27-31` is already file-agnostic (it reads 20 lines and matches the marker). Cut the new helper, rename the existing one (for example `hasManagedMarker`), and call it per file. The project's own `CLAUDE.md:17` says "Do not duplicate logic."

findings.title: Guide-script backend is one bullet with no automated test
Cross-repo rollout and the old-guide failure path are named as a risk but not handled
findings.description:
Files Changed lists a file in a different repository (`.gitmodules:3`). The design gives no landing order, no submodule pointer bump, and no minimum-guide check.

Walking it as an operator on an existing installation with a pinned older guide:
1. `cf setup-ide copilot` first prompts and writes `.bak` backups.
2. The script then rejects the target. The in-tree copy does this at `project-documents/scripts/setup-ide:301-310` with "Unsupported IDE", exit 1.
3. The CLI reports only "setup-ide exited with code 1" (`setup-ide.ts:99-102`), with no pointer to `cf guides update`.

Via `cf init --ide copilot` the failure is downgraded to a warning and followed by "Your project is ready" (`init.ts:113-120`). The "clear error" on line 133 is not what the code produces. Specify the remediation message, and run the script-support check before the backup step.

findings.title: `applyTo` translation leaves the alwaysApply rule and the plan's "both forms" undefined
Same always-on content is written to two (or three) files Copilot loads together
findings.description:
The decision is justified as a "single compiled file", but it then writes identical content to `AGENTS.md`. The referenced tool guide states both are always-on in workspace chat (`project-documents/user/tool-guides/copilot-vscode/setup-ide.md:18`, `:26`). It also states VS Code reads `CLAUDE.md` and `.claude/rules` (`:18`, `:33`). A dual-target project therefore sends the compiled rules up to three times, plus duplicated scoped rules.

The plan requires both files to exist (lines 189, 211) but words the content as "`copilot-instructions.md` (or `AGENTS.md`)" (line 201). The design should make one file authoritative and the other a short pointer, and state the dual-target behaviour.

findings.title: Stale generated files are never removed
findings.description: When a rule or skill is renamed or removed upstream, the old `.github/instructions/X.instructions.md` or `.github/prompts/X.prompt.md` stays in the root and in every worktree. Propagation only copies (`setup-ide.ts:150-153`). Copilot keeps auto-applying the stale file, which conflicts with plan line 201 ("narrowly scoped and non-conflicting"). Only manual deletion ends that state. The managed marker already makes safe pruning possible; the design should say the script (and propagation) deletes managed files it no longer generates.

findings.title: Two plan-assigned items are dropped
findings.description:
- **Tool guide reference:** plan lines 184 and 218 require the tool guide (`project-documents/user/tool-guides/copilot-vscode/setup-ide.md`) to be referenced in the slice design and promoted if needed. The design never mentions it. The file is a raw chat export (`:1-3`), so the promotion decision is live.
- **Agents mapping:** plan line 192 assigns "document mapping" for `.claude/agents` → custom agents. Line 54 promises to "document the mapping", but no mapping appears anywhere in the design.

findings.title: Propagation and prompt tests cannot be written as described
findings.description:
- `propagateToWorktrees` is module-private (`setup-ide.ts:127`), so it cannot be called with `target = 'copilot'` directly.
- `packages/cli/tests/commands/setup-ide.test.ts` has no worktree test today. Its fs mock (`:27-41`) covers only `existsSync`, `copyFileSync` and `readFileSync`, and `sampleProject` (`:47-51`) has no `worktrees`.
- The "prompts before overwriting" case (line 125) has no precedent: no existing test drives `askConfirmation` or readline.

The design should say whether to export the function or test through the command, and which mocks are added. It should also state that the copilot block must `mkdir` `.github/` in each worktree before copying.

findings.title: Help text and docs
findings.description: The `setup-ide` argument help is derived from `VALID_TARGETS` (`setup-ide.ts:167`), so it updates on its own. `cf init --help` says only "default: claude" (`init.ts:44`), and the design freezes `init.ts` (line 117). `README.md:66,154` and `packages/cli/README.md:122,224` list only `claude` and are not in Files Changed.

findings.title: `cf init --ide copilot` still installs Claude slash commands
findings.description: `installCommandsAction()` runs for every IDE target and writes to `~/.claude/commands/cf/` (`commandInstaller.ts:90-93`). A Copilot-only user gets a `~/.claude` tree and no `/cf:*` equivalents under `.github/prompts/`. This is outside the plan's scope for 210, but it qualifies the "end-to-end" claim on line 33.

findings.title: Sequence ordering and init-path propagation
findings.description: In code, "IDE setup complete" prints inside `setupIdeAction` (`setup-ide.ts:105`) before propagation (`:195`), the reverse of steps 6 and 7. Propagation happens only in the `cf setup-ide` handler. `cf init --ide copilot` on an already-registered project with worktrees (`init.ts:63-65`, `:111`) will not propagate. That is consistent with plan line 215 ("after root setup-ide") but worth stating.

findings.title: The "VS Code strips markers" risk can be cut
findings.description: VS Code reads instruction files; it does not rewrite them on disk, so the described degradation has no mechanism. Technical Scope (28-34), Interfaces (87-91) and Files Changed (107-111) also restate the same four edits three times. One list would do.
